text:
anna: seeing a regressed tail on the embeddings-reranker non-chat endpoint after the kernel-selector + new batcher landed. p99 jumped from ~420ms to ~860ms on nightly runs. not all pods, seems correlated with high-embed-token requests and prefill bursts.

raj: can you paste the perf numbers and which commit landed?

anna: yep. nightly perf (canary stack): p50 110ms, p95 320ms, p99 860ms. baseline before change: p50 95ms, p95 280ms, p99 420ms. commit is 7f3a2c1 kernel-selection: prefer-int8-kernel when seq_len<=64 + batcher: greedy-balancer v1.2.

maria: interesting. greedy-balancer tries to max-fill windows which could be increasing kv-cache churn if requests with similar prefixes are split across batches. any kv cache eviction spikes?

anna: yes, saw KV_CACHE evict rate increase ~3x. small snippet from profiler: 

```
KVCache: capacity=20k entries, evictions=3100/s (prev=980/s)
Batcher: avg_batch_size=12 -> 18 (after change)
Kernel: selected=int8_fast_seq<=64 (fallback kernel used for longer seqs)
TokenBudgetTarget: 2048 (same as baseline)
```

bob: avg batch size up is expected, but higher evictions means the K/V working set is being thrash-prefilled. if the batcher combines heterogeneous prefixes, the KV hits go down and each request misses, hitting slower kernels or fallback. where is kernel fallback happening? logs?

anna: stack from slow request: 

```
[2026-03-16T23:11:02Z] request_id=rid-cc239
batch_id=bid-41
selected_kernel=int8_fast_seq<=64
on_step=kv_lookup -> miss -> fallback_kernel=torch_generic
latency_breakdown: kv_lookup=75ms, kernel_exec=220ms, batching_wait=45ms
```

maria: fallback to torch_generic is the killer. int8_fast has a narrow working set; when KV misses force full compute path we pay more. two angles: reduce greedy merging across dissimilar keys, or increase token_budget_target so more of the prefix fits in KV cache TTL.

raj: increasing token_budget seems odd — token budget is about per-batch token cap, not cache size. but larger token budget can increase batch token count and may reduce per-token overhead if kernels are better for longer sequences. still feels like orthogonal.

bob: quick experiment idea: run two canaries with same kernel selection but different batch formation heuristics: (A) greedy-balancer (current), (B) prefix-aware packer (pack by hashed prefix_id, avoid merging different tenants/queries). see which reduces KV miss rate. also add kv-cache TTL bump + prefetch backoff.

anna: I can spin those. patch for (B) is small: change batcher policy to prefer same prefix hash within window and limit cross-prefix merges to <2 per batch. patch: 

```
batch_policy:
  type: prefix_aware_packer
  window_ms: 12
  max_cross_prefix: 2
  early_fill_ratio: 0.15
```

devops-bot: deploy requested by anna for cluster canary-emb-regen (2 pods) at 2026-03-17T00:05Z. CI passed.

maria: also add a histogram for kernel_fallback_reason into runtime tracing. we only have boolean fallback today. need reasons: kv_miss, seq_len_mismatch, unsupported_layout.

raj: agree. add metrics: kernel_fallback_reason{kv_miss|seq_len|layout} and batch_prefix_entropy. that will help.

anna: ran the canaries for 30m. preliminary numbers: prefix-aware packer (B): p99 480ms, KV evict rate down to 1.1k/s. greedy-balancer (A): p99 820ms, KV evict 3.2k/s. kernel_fallback_reason shows kv_miss dominated for A.

bob: those are promising. can we tune early_fill_ratio lower to avoid starving latency with small prefixes? B's p95 is slightly worse (B p95 330ms vs A p95 310ms).

maria: tradeoff looks acceptable: small p95 blip for big p99 wins. next: test with token_budget_target variations (1k, 2k, 4k) to find sweet spot. also try bumping KV cache capacity by 25% for the canary pods.

anna: running parameter grid now. rough plan: 3x canaries: (B, token=2048, kvcap+25%), (B, token=1024, kvcap+25%), (B, token=4096, kvcap+25%). will collect p50/95/99 + kv evict + kernel_fallback_reason.

raj: also collect per-model kernel selection distribution. if int8_fast is being chosen incorrectly for some shapes that then fallback, maybe tighten selector rule: require prefix_kv_hit_rate>0.6 to pick int8_fast.

bob: good call. fallback reasons + prefix_hit_rate gating seems robust.

maria: action items: 
- anna: run the 3 canaries and post perf table (owner: anna)
- raj: add kernel_fallback_reason and batch_prefix_entropy metrics to telemetry (owner: raj)
- bob: prototype selector gate based on prefix_kv_hit_rate (>0.6) (owner: bob)
- maria: run regression test with stress harness for 2h (owner: maria)

anna: logging results as I get them. initial canary (B, token=2048, kvcap+25%) shows steady p99 ~450ms after 15m. will post full table in ~45m.

raj: thanks. if B + kvcap solves 90% of p99, we should roll to canary fleet and keep kernel selector change but add the prefix-aware packer and gating.

bob: if we do roll, add a quick feature-flag so we can revert packer behavior without redeploy.

anna: noted. will submit the FF and canary rollout plan.

devops-bot: deployment canary-emb-regen (B variant) complete: pods ready.

anna: update after 1h grid run: summary table: 

```
Variant A (greedy, token=2048, kvcap): p50 115 p95 325 p99 820 kv_evict 3200/s
Variant B1 (prefix, token=2048, kvcap+25%): p50 118 p95 330 p99 450 kv_evict 1100/s
Variant B2 (prefix, token=1024, kvcap+25%): p50 120 p95 340 p99 510 kv_evict 1300/s
Variant B3 (prefix, token=4096, kvcap+25%): p50 112 p95 308 p99 430 kv_evict 1050/s
```

anna: takeaways: prefix-aware packer consistently halves p99 and reduces KV evictions. increasing token_budget to 4096 improved p50/p95 slightly and p99 marginally over 2048. kvcap bump helped but not required for correctness.

maria: nice. next steps: roll prefix-aware packer to staging canary fleet and enable selector gate (prefix_kv_hit_rate>0.6) behind flag. schedule 6h stress.

raj: I'll land the metrics PR and add dashboards for fallback reasons.

bob: I'll push selector gate MR and add unit tests.

anna: closing loop: main regression seems caused by greedy-balancer mixing prefixes which increased KV miss rate and triggered costly fallback kernels. fix is combination of prefix-aware batch formation + kernel selector gating + optional token_budget tuning.

maria: cool — thanks team. :thumbsup:

bob: nice win.

anna: filing followup doc with perf plots and the config diffs. will link here when ready.
